judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: h2 'Let the Christmas Magic Begin!' over a carousel of products from /collections/christmas-gifts (handmade chocolates box, iced Christmas cake, Christmas pudding, advent calendar, glass tree ornaments, a Christmas stocking, a gingerbread cup). claimTrue: no. The heading does say something about the content: it is Christmas-themed, and so is every item under it. elementFails: leaning no. 2.4.6 asks headings to describe the topic, not to be precise; under G130 this heading names the section's theme, though not the fact that these are gifts to buy. captureDiffers: no. The live HTML has the same heading and section. Competent auditors would reasonably disagree on whether a slogan heading that names only the season is descriptive enough, so the label is uncertain.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Header search field (input type=search, role combobox, name 'Search') whose placeholder a script cycles through 'Search for throws...', 'Search for hampers...' and 'Search for scarves...' (the data-placeholder attributes; the capture caught it mid-typing as 'Search for scarve'). claimTrue: yes. The quoted string is one of the cycled placeholders, and the colours hold: the live main.css sets .search__input::placeholder to the text colour at 50% alpha, and the screenshot's placeholder pixels are #979697 on #ececec, 2.49:1, at 16px normal weight. elementFails: yes. The placeholder is the only visible text saying what the field is for (the 'Search' label is not shown), so it is not incidental, and 2.49:1 is below 1.4.3's 4.5:1. I found no technique or exception that would make it pass. captureDiffers: no. The live HTML and CSS give the same placeholder strings and the same placeholder colour rule.
